page.layout: One page of running text, one column, with the running head at the top and the page number above it. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Quotus enim quisque nostrûm est, qui Ecclesiæ & totius & singulorū piorū calamitates intuens, nō ita argumentetur:
Non æquū est, sic tractari homines fi-deles, luce Euangelij illustratos, & eius propagandi studiosos, ut Pontificios aliósue osores doctrinæ Euangelicæ.
Nos uero sideles sumus, luce Euange-lij illustrati, ac doctrinæ lampadem per manus tradere posteris constitutum ha-bemus.
Quare non æquum esse uidetur, ut cō-munibus malis, publicè grassantibus, & quæ idolomania meretur & accersit, ipsi quoque inuoluamur.

Atqui, si rem rectè reputauerimus, idē ferè de nobis dici posse animaduertemus, quod de Iudæis Paulus pronuncia-uit, Rom.2.v.17. & sequentibus. Quor-sum autem attinet de Euangelio, de fide, de excusso Antichristi iugo gloriari, cum interim fructus pœnitentia dignos non proferentes, Deum turpi nostra uita dedecoremus? Proderit quidem nobis E-uangelium, proderunt & Sacramenta, si fide per charitatem agete, Dei nomé san-ctificauerimus: at si Deum nos sci[?]pro-fesi[?]

page.notes: Line 1 of the page: the first word "Quotus" shows the printer's Q with a possible overbar; read as printed. In the last line a printer's ornament (a small diamond or blot) stands after "sci", so the letters there are uncertain: "sci[?]". The word broken at the foot of the page ("pro-" / "fefsi") is read as "profesi[?]"; the second line is faint. The running head is read as HYPOMNEMATA; the E may carry an accent. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout.
